info.title: ZROtext sealed API v1 (proposed contract)
info.description: CONTRACT WITH DEFAULT-OFF IMPLEMENTED SLICES, derived from ZT-009 decisions recorded 2026-09-26. IMPLEMENTED: POST /v1/sealed/messages, POST /v1/sealed/inbound-events, metadata-only message list/status/pre-grant cancellation, and the read-only devices, webhook metadata/delivery metadata and usage resource groups. All are mounted only under SEALED_ADMISSION_ENABLED; the runtime is disabled by default. Admission/upload require exact raw binary envelopes; lifecycle operations never expose content or recipient fields. Existing slice-2 resource handlers and tests define their current projections; the prospective resource schemas here are not evidence that every proposed field or error is implemented. PROPOSAL ONLY: webhook mutations and remaining prospective resource behavior; no server route implements those proposals. Ciphertext retrieval, negotiated grants and outbound dispatch-status fanout remain deferred. The synthetic-alpha plane and stable general-send plane stay separate. There is no JSON/plaintext admission, downgrade, fallback translation, implicit reader or carrier-delivery evidence. All implemented responses are no-store.

post.summary: Submit one sealed outbound envelope for device dispatch
post.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. The request body is exactly one complete sealed outbound envelope (profile kind 01) as raw binary bytes with the exact content type application/vnd.zrotext.sealed.v1. The relay never decrypts: it verifies the owner-pinned manifest chain, the allowed device signing key and scope, and the device signature over the exact unsigned bytes, then compares the protected account/device/line/manifest fields with the authenticated identity and database state. Idempotency is the SHA-256 digest of the unsigned envelope bytes (Q6): an identical replay returns the stored message identity with created=false and performs no new dispatch; no caller-supplied idempotency-key header is accepted. Admission fails closed when the active manifest is expired or was issued too far in the future (Q4), and clock-rollback or restored-high-water conditions require fresh owner-verified enrollment (Q4). The plaintext inside the ciphertext is a strict UTF-8 body of 1-32,768 bytes with no BOM, no NUL, no Unicode normalization and no padding in v1 (Q9); body length, recipient, timing and segment-count leakage is disclosed and accepted. Every response carries Cache-Control: no-store.

requestBody.description: One complete sealed outbound envelope (kind 01) as raw bytes. Bounds: the envelope is at least 426 bytes, at most 34,213 bytes for kind 01, and the request-body limit is the 36,864-byte pre-allocation cap. A JSON body, any other content type, an unknown profile or kind, a set downgrade flag, or trailing bytes is rejected (Q11).

202.description: Accepted for dispatch, or an identical replay no-op. Acceptance means durable storage of the exact envelope bytes and queueing toward the bound device; it never means carrier submission. Idempotency is on the unsigned envelope digest (Q6): replaying byte-identical unsigned content returns the existing message identity with created=false.

400.description: invalid_request: the bytes are not a bounded, exactly parsed sealed envelope, or verification of the manifest chain, signing key/scope or device signature failed, or a client-allocated identity is malformed. future_manifest: the manifest's issued_at is more than five minutes ahead of trusted server time (Q4); resubmitting unchanged will not help until the manifest is reissued.

401.description: unauthorized: missing, malformed or unknown bearer credential.

403.description: forbidden: the credential is not authorized for the tenant, line or device named in the envelope, or the key is revoked or wrong-role. stale_manifest: the active manifest has expired (its exclusive expiry passed, or its lifetime exceeds 24 hours), which blocks sealed outbound fail-closed until a fresh manifest is pinned (Q4). re_enrollment_required: a device-clock rollback or a restored high-water store was detected; sealed submission stays refused until fresh owner-verified enrollment (Q4).

409.description: idempotency_conflict: a client-allocated identity in the protected record was already stored under a different unsigned envelope digest (Q6); the earlier envelope stays authoritative and this submission creates nothing.

415.description: unsupported_media_type: the request did not use exactly application/vnd.zrotext.sealed.v1. A JSON body, a multipart body, or any other content type is rejected here and is never parsed as a sealed envelope, translated to the synthetic-alpha route, or retried as plaintext (Q11).

429.description: rate_limited, queue_full or quota_exceeded: the account or device exceeded its sealed admission budget.

503.description: unavailable or billing_pending: storage or dispatch is temporarily unavailable; retry later with the same envelope bytes.

get.description: messages:read. Twenty newest records ordered by (created_at,id), with one optional exclusive cursor resolved inside the same account/device/transport visibility. Foreign/deleted cursor is indistinguishable from absent. Existing sealed queue identity; no new queue, admission verifier, plaintext alternative or dispatch enablement. Mounted only behind SEALED_ADMISSION_ENABLED, disabled by default. Credentials are revalidated under transaction locks; account/device-bound visibility matches current scopes. Metadata only, no envelope or recipient fields. Cache-Control: no-store.

200.description: Current stored metadata; cancellation is idempotent.

400.description: invalid_request: malformed UUID/query or nonempty cancellation body

401.description: unauthorized: missing, malformed, expired or revoked bearer

403.description: forbidden: wrong scope or authority changed after authentication

404.description: not_found: disabled route, absent, foreign, wrong-device or non-sealed identity/cursor

post.summary: Upload one sealed inbound event captured by a device
post.description: Mounted behind the default-off SEALED_ADMISSION_ENABLED flag exactly like the message route: when the flag is off the path answers 404 before reading any body or credential. This is the separate sealed inbound route required by Q8: it writes the separate sealed_inbound_events store and must never be routed through the M1 outbound-attempt inbound pilot. The request body is exactly one complete sealed inbound envelope (profile kind 02) as raw binary bytes with the exact content type application/vnd.zrotext.sealed.v1. The phone allocates one stable 16-byte event_id for the normalized logical SMS, journals text, event ID and a positive device-local sequence before sealing, and retries replay the exact envelope bytes. The server compares the (account, device, event_id) identity and the (device, device_sequence) replay fence against the unsigned envelope digest: an identical replay is a no-op success with created=false; a changed event under the same identity or a reused device sequence fails with 409. Out-of-order arrival is accepted within a seven-day observed-time window (Q8). Tombstone retention is an operational constraint: event-ID and device-sequence tombstones must be retained at least eight days after first acceptance, because deleting a row without a durable fence would permit replay. When the active manifest is expired the device quarantines the event locally until a fresh manifest rather than uploading (Q4); if an expired-manifest upload still arrives, the server fails closed. Clock-rollback or restored-high-water conditions require fresh owner-verified enrollment (Q4). The plaintext inside the ciphertext is a strict UTF-8 body of 1-32,768 bytes with no BOM, no NUL, no Unicode normalization and no padding in v1 (Q9). Every response carries Cache-Control: no-store and never echoes envelope content.

requestBody.description: One complete sealed inbound envelope (kind 02) as raw bytes. Bounds: the envelope is at least 426 bytes, at most 34,082 bytes for kind 02, and the request-body limit is the 36,864-byte pre-allocation cap. A JSON body, any other content type, an unknown profile or kind, or a set downgrade flag is rejected (Q11).

202.description: Stored, or an identical replay no-op. created=false means this exact (account, device, event_id) with the same unsigned digest was already accepted and nothing new was created. Out-of-order arrival is accepted within the seven-day observed-time window (Q8). Acceptance is durable storage only; ciphertext-only fanout of accepted events is specified by the sealed webhook delivery contract (SealedWebhookEventBody) and remains unimplemented.

400.description: invalid_request: the bytes are not a bounded, exactly parsed sealed envelope, or verification of the manifest chain, signing key/scope or device signature failed. future_manifest: the manifest's issued_at is more than five minutes ahead of trusted server time (Q4). stale_event: the observed time falls outside the seven-day observed-time window (Q8).

401.description: unauthorized: missing, malformed or unknown bearer credential.

403.description: forbidden: the credential is not authorized for the tenant, line or device named in the protected record, the line binding is not active at the current generation, or the key is revoked or wrong-role. stale_manifest: the manifest has expired; the device should have quarantined the event locally until a fresh manifest (Q4), and the server fails closed. re_enrollment_required: a device-clock rollback or a restored high-water store was detected; upload stays refused until fresh owner-verified enrollment (Q4).

409.description: event_id_conflict: this event_id was already accepted for the account and device with a different unsigned digest (changed content). sequence_conflict: this (device, device_sequence) was already consumed by a different event. Both are conflicting replays under the Q8 fences; the stored event stays authoritative and the conflicting upload creates nothing.

415.description: unsupported_media_type: the request did not use exactly application/vnd.zrotext.sealed.v1. A JSON body, a multipart body, or any other content type is rejected here and is never parsed as a sealed envelope, translated to the synthetic-alpha route, or retried as plaintext (Q11).

429.description: rate_limited, queue_full or quota_exceeded: the account or device exceeded its sealed admission budget.

503.description: unavailable or billing_pending: storage is temporarily unavailable; retry later with the exact same envelope bytes, event ID and sequence.

get.summary: List the account's enrolled devices with their sealed line bindings
get.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. Read-only projection of the owner enrollment view onto the sealed API-key plane: one cursor page of the account's enrolled devices with revocation state, the current active_socket_lease observation, and each device's sealed-purpose line bindings (line_id, binding_generation, state) from the device_line_bindings table. Cursor pagination mirrors the owner route GET /v1/enrollment/devices: pass the returned next_cursor as before to fetch the next page; next_cursor is null after the last page. This surface never enrolls, approves, re-keys or revokes a device: pairing, owner approval and revocation stay on the owner-session enrollment routes because the Q1/Q4 ceremonies are out-of-band owner actions. No SIM identifier, phone number, ICCID, IMSI, Android subscription ID or key material is ever returned. Sealed-mode eligibility (Android API 31+, Q5) is a device property the owner verifies at enrollment; this list reports stored state only. Every response carries Cache-Control: no-store.

get.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. The sealed-profile projection of the owner webhook lifecycle (protocol/v1/webhook-endpoints.md) onto API-key authentication with the webhooks:read scope. Returns every endpoint of this account (at most eight, including disabled ones) ordered by creation. Never includes signing secrets or encrypted secret bytes; only the create and rotate responses ever expose a secret, once per generated secret. paused_at_ms and failure_started_at_ms expose the 72-hour sustained-transport-failure pause exactly as the owner list does. post.summary: Create one disabled webhook endpoint for sealed event fanout
post.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. Creates a disabled endpoint exactly as the owner-session POST /v1/webhooks does, returning the endpoint view plus the signing secret exactly once. The callback URL must pass the strict egress validator used by the owner route: an HTTPS DNS name on port 443, at most 2048 bytes, no IP literals, no userinfo, no fragment, no local/internal/special-use names and no invalid host labels; the URL is revalidated on enable and the resolved addresses are re-checked and pinned on every delivery attempt. The signing secret is 32 random bytes returned as unpadded base64url and is never retrievable again: only an AES-256-GCM ciphertext bound to account, endpoint and key version is stored, and losing the response requires rotation. The account cap is eight endpoints including disabled ones (409 endpoint_limit). Sealed event bodies delivered to this endpoint carry only ciphertext and metadata (see SealedWebhookEventBody); no route sends a test webhook, and no synthetic-alpha content is ever fanned out (Q11). Enabling actual delivery stays a separate operational gate. Cache-Control: no-store.

requestBody.description: The callback URL. Unknown JSON members are rejected.

201.description: Endpoint created disabled. The signing secret appears in this response and in the rotate response only; there is no retrieval route.

400.description: invalid_request: the JSON body is malformed, not sent as application/json, has unknown or missing members, or has a member of the wrong type. invalid_webhook_endpoint: the callback URL fails the strict HTTPS egress validator.

get.summary: Page delivery history for one webhook endpoint
get.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. Read-only delivery and attempt metadata for this account's endpoint, mirroring the owner history route. Optional limit (1-20, default 20) and before (the delivery_id returned as next_before on the preceding page); ordered newest first by creation time then ID; attempts from every generation, including retired deliveries, are included as immutable audit history. No payload, callback URL, signing secret, response body, recipient, sender or inbound/sealed content is ever returned: event bodies stay ciphertext-only and this route returns none of them. An unknown or another account's endpoint or cursor is 404 not_found; invalid IDs and page sizes are 400. Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.description: Cursor: the delivery_id returned as next_before on the preceding page.

post.summary: Queue one bounded replay generation of an exhausted failed delivery
post.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. Mirrors the owner manual-replay contract. The caller generates a random UUIDv4 Idempotency-Key and must reuse the exact same key after an uncertain response; the server never generates one on the caller's behalf. The endpoint must be enabled and the delivery must be dead with terminal_reason failed after seven completed transport failures in its current generation; pending, leased, succeeded, policy-rejected, retired and legacy rows are ineligible (409 replay_not_eligible), as is reusing the same key for a different delivery. A delivery has at most three generations (409 replay_limit): the initial seven attempts and two replay generations of seven attempts each (retry schedule 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h after each failure). Repeating a successful request returns 202 with the same generation and created:false. This action only queues work; the delivery sender remains a separate operational gate, and because a previous timeout may already have reached the receiver, the receiver must still deduplicate the event_id across every generation. Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.name: delivery_id
parameters.description: The exhausted failed delivery to replay.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A caller-generated random UUIDv4, durable across HTTP retries and never server-generated. Reuse the exact key after an uncertain response; using it for another delivery is a conflict.

202.description: Replay generation queued, or an identical idempotent replay no-op (created:false with the same generation, even if that generation has since run).

400.description: invalid_request: the Idempotency-Key is absent, malformed or not a UUIDv4, or a path ID is malformed.

401.description: unauthorized: missing, malformed or unknown bearer credential.

403.description: forbidden: the credential lacks the webhooks:manage scope or is bound to a different tenant.

404.description: not_found: no such endpoint or delivery in this account.

409.description: replay_not_eligible: the delivery is not an exhausted failed generation, the endpoint is disabled, or the Idempotency-Key was already used for a different delivery. replay_limit: the delivery already used all three generations.

503.description: unavailable: storage is temporarily unavailable; retry later with the same Idempotency-Key.

post.summary: Enable future sealed event fanout to one endpoint
post.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. Revalidates the callback URL against the strict egress validator and the decryptability of the stored signing secret, then enables future fan-out and clears any transport-failure pause, exactly as the owner enable route does. Enabling never replays work retired by disable or rotation: only sealed events accepted while the endpoint is enabled create new deliveries. Actual sending remains a separate operational gate. No request body. Cache-Control: no-store.

post.summary: Disable an endpoint and permanently retire its pending deliveries
post.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. Disables the endpoint and permanently retires its pending and leased deliveries in one transaction, exactly as the owner disable route does. Completed deliveries remain as audit history; retired deliveries can never be replayed, and re-enabling cannot revive them. An in-flight HTTPS request that already loaded a payload may still complete, so the receiver must deduplicate the event_id. No request body. Cache-Control: no-store.

post.summary: Rotate the signing secret, disabling the endpoint and retiring its deliveries
post.description: Proposed contract; no route exists. Generates a new 32-byte signing secret, disables the endpoint and permanently retires pending, leased and replayable failed deliveries in one transaction, exactly as the owner rotate route does. The new secret is returned as unpadded base64url exactly once; only the AES-256-GCM ciphertext bound to account, endpoint and key version is stored, and there is no retrieval route. Receivers should keep verifying with the old secret until deliveries signed with the new secret arrive. No request body. Cache-Control: no-store.

200.description: Secret rotated; endpoint disabled and its pending deliveries permanently retired. The new signing secret appears here and in the create response only.

get.description: Read-only query of the single authoritative metering core (usage_periods and usage_ledger) for the authenticated account: bounded pages of UTC calendar-month periods, newest first, each with its unit limit, reserved units, refunded units and the derived used units (reserved - refunded). Counter semantics are fixed: reserved counts accepted messages, reserved in the same transaction as admission; refunds exist only through the pre-grant cancellation/expiry path, are written exactly once per message against the original period, and an idempotent digest replay reuses the original reservation. used units is a reservation counter and is never a submitted or delivered counter. Units are integer counts of accepted messages, never currency, invoices or per-recipient pricing. Per-device or per-line breakdowns do not exist and are not implied. The metric stays the shared outbound_message unit in v1.

200.description: One bounded page of usage periods; empty history is an empty page.

401.description: unauthorized: missing, malformed or unknown bearer credential.

403.description: forbidden: the credential lacks the billing:read scope or is bound to a different tenant.

503.description: unavailable or billing_pending: usage storage or billing reconciliation is temporarily unavailable; retry later.

400.description: invalid_request: out-of-bounds limit or malformed before cursor.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from a previous next_before: return periods with period_start strictly before this date. Malformed or calendrically impossible values are invalid_request.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Periods per page, 1 to 24, default 12. Out-of-bounds is invalid_request.

Stale manifest/line never reauthorizes sending; historical metadata remains readable. Existing sealed queue identity; no new queue, admission verifier, plaintext alternative or dispatch enablement. Mounted only behind SEALED_ADMISSION_ENABLED, disabled by default. Credentials are revalidated under transaction locks; account/device-bound visibility matches current scopes. Metadata only, no envelope or recipient fields. Cache-Control: no-store.

post.description: messages:send. Empty body. Serialize on the existing dispatch job then message locks against grant publication, cancel only pre-grant states, close lease and refund original reservation once atomically. Repeated cancelled state is a no-op; expired/granted/unknown work is 409. Historical manifest/line staleness does not prevent removing ungranted work, and never bypasses admission or authorizes a new grant. Existing sealed queue identity; no new queue, admission verifier, plaintext alternative or dispatch enablement. Mounted only behind SEALED_ADMISSION_ENABLED, disabled by default. Credentials are revalidated under transaction locks; account/device-bound visibility matches current scopes. Metadata only, no envelope or recipient fields. Cache-Control: no-store.

400.description: invalid_request: malformed UUID/query or nonempty cancellation body

401.description: unauthorized: missing, malformed, expired or revoked bearer

403.description: forbidden: wrong scope or authority changed after authentication

404.description: not_found: disabled route, absent, foreign, wrong-device or non-sealed identity/cursor

409.description: cancellation_conflict: expired, irreversible grant or other non-cancellable evidence; no refund or radio cancellation inference

bearerAuth.description: The existing customer API-key authentication, not a new auth model: an account API key issued by the owner API-key routes under /v1/auth and sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>', exactly as the existing message routes authenticate. Outbound submission requires the existing message-send scope bound to the device named in the envelope's protected record; inbound upload requires a credential authorized for the uploading device, and the protected account, device and line fields must match the authenticated identity and the active line-binding generation. The slice 2 resource operations reuse the existing scope set and add no new scopes: devices list/status requires devices:read, webhook reads require webhooks:read, webhook management (create, replay, enable, disable, rotate) requires webhooks:manage, and the usage query requires billing:read. API keys never unlock content: no scope grants decryption, plaintext access or envelope bytes beyond the exact bytes a caller itself submitted. This HTTP layer only names the tenant: the sealed manifest chain and device signature over the exact unsigned bytes carry the cryptographic authorization (Q2, Q7). Sealed and alpha credentials stay separate (Q11).

NoStore.description: Every sealed response is non-cacheable, mirroring the existing message routes.

SealedEnvelopeBytes.description: One complete sealed envelope as raw binary bytes: the exact profile bytes including the fixed prefix, protected record, body ciphertext, recipient wraps and signature. Never JSON, never base64-wrapped, never a multipart part. The encrypted plaintext is a strict UTF-8 body of 1-32,768 bytes with no BOM, no NUL, no Unicode normalization and no padding in v1 (Q9).

SealedOutboundAccepted.description: Acceptance metadata for a sealed outbound envelope. Contains no recipient, no plaintext and no envelope bytes.

message_id.description: The server-allocated message identity for the accepted envelope; identical on digest replays.

created.description: false when this exact unsigned envelope digest was already accepted (idempotent replay, Q6).

SealedInboundAccepted.description: Acceptance metadata for a sealed inbound event. Contains no sender, no plaintext and no envelope bytes.

event_id.description: The phone-allocated stable event identity echoed back from the protected record.

created.description: false when this exact (account, device, event_id) with the same unsigned digest was already accepted (no-op replay, Q8).

SealedDeviceLine.description: One sealed-purpose line binding of a device, from the device_line_bindings rows with purpose 'sealed'. A phone line is a stable owner-assigned identity, never an Android subscription ID, SIM slot, phone number, ICCID or IMSI.

binding_generation.description: The binding generation of this row. Sealed authorization must bind the active line-binding generation (Q7); rebinding after a SIM move increments it.

state.description: Binding state. At most one active binding exists per line; revoked bindings never return to pending or active.

SealedDevice.description: One enrolled device of the account and its sealed-purpose line bindings. Read-only view; contains no SIM identifier, phone number, ICCID, IMSI, Android subscription ID or key material.

device_id.description: The enrolled device identity assigned at pairing.

display_name.description: Owner-assigned label chosen at enrollment; free-form text, not a phone number or serial.

revoked.description: True once the owner revoked the device; revoked devices never appear active on the device stream.

active_socket_lease.description: Snapshot observation of the authoritative writer's current authenticated device session: true only while the lease is unexpired, the session deployment epoch is current, and the hosting site is enabled and not draining. A dropped socket can stay represented until its 90-second lease expires; this is not a continuous connection monitor and establishes neither SMS permission, SIM state, carrier service nor radio readiness.

lines.description: The device's sealed-purpose line bindings. Empty when the device has none.

SealedDevicePage.description: One cursor page of the account's devices.

next_cursor.description: The device_id to pass as before on the next request; null after the last page.

SealedWebhookCreateRequest.description: Create request for one webhook endpoint. Unknown members are rejected. The callback URL must pass the strict egress validator: HTTPS DNS name on port 443, at most 2048 bytes, no IP literals, userinfo, fragments, local/internal/special-use names or invalid host labels.

callback_url.description: The HTTPS URL sealed event deliveries are posted to.

SealedWebhookEndpoint.description: One webhook endpoint of the account. Never includes signing secrets or encrypted secret bytes.

enabled.description: Whether sealed events accepted now create new deliveries for this endpoint.

paused_at_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when the sender paused the endpoint after 72 hours of sustained transport failure; null while unpause. Pending deliveries stay queued and the sender skips the endpoint while this is set.

failure_started_at_ms.description: Unix milliseconds of the first failure of the current streak; null when the last delivery was acknowledged.

SealedWebhookEndpointList.description: All of the account's webhook endpoints, at most eight, ordered by creation.

endpoints.description: The account's endpoints, including disabled ones.

SealedWebhookSecret.description: Create/rotate response exposing the signing secret exactly once per generated secret. Only an AES-256-GCM ciphertext bound to account, endpoint and key version is stored; there is no retrieval route, and losing this response requires rotation.

enabled.description: Always false in this response: a created endpoint starts disabled, and rotation disables the endpoint.

signing_secret_b64url.description: 32 random bytes as unpadded base64url. Decode to raw bytes for HMAC-SHA256 verification of the x-zrotext-signature delivery header.

SealedWebhookDeliveryAttempt.description: One completed or in-flight delivery attempt of the current or an earlier generation. Immutable audit history; contains no payload or response body.

generation.description: The generation this attempt belongs to: the initial generation or one of at most two replay generations.

attempt_number.description: The attempt's position within its generation (at most seven attempts per generation).

started_at_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when the sender leased this attempt.

completed_at_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when the attempt finished; null while in flight.

outcome.description: The transport outcome; null while in flight.

http_status.description: The receiver's HTTP status when one was received; null otherwise.

SealedWebhookDelivery.description: Delivery metadata for one sealed event fan-out. No payload, callback URL, signing secret, response body, recipient or content is ever included.

event_id.description: The stable sealed event identity being delivered; the receiver deduplicates on this value across generations.

status.description: Delivery state. dead means terminal after exhaustion, policy rejection or retirement.

generation.description: The current generation: initial plus at most two manual replays.

terminal_reason.description: Set exactly when status is dead; null otherwise.

attempt_count.description: Completed attempts in the current generation.

next_attempt_at_ms.description: Unix milliseconds of the next retry; present only while pending, null otherwise. Retry schedule per generation: 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h after each failure.

updated_at_ms.description: Unix milliseconds of the last state change.

attempts.description: Attempts of every generation in order, including retired deliveries.

SealedWebhookDeliveryPage.description: One page of delivery history, newest first by creation time then ID.

next_before.description: The delivery_id to pass as before on the next request; null after the last page.

SealedWebhookReplayAccepted.description: Acceptance metadata for one bounded replay request. Contains no payload and no receiver data.

delivery_id.description: The delivery a new generation was queued for.

generation.description: The newly queued replay generation, or the existing generation on an idempotent replay with created false.

created.description: false when this exact Idempotency-Key was already honored (same generation returned).

SealedWebhookEventBody.description: PROPOSED outbound body the delivery sender POSTs to the customer's callback URL for one accepted sealed inbound event. This is not a response of any API operation in this document. Ciphertext-only fanout: envelope_b64 carries the exact stored sealed envelope bytes and the relay never decrypts, never synthesizes plaintext and never substitutes synthetic-alpha content (Q11). Delivered with content type application/json and the headers x-zrotext-timestamp (ASCII Unix seconds) and x-zrotext-signature ('v1=' plus lowercase hex of HMAC-SHA256(timestamp || '.' || exact raw body) keyed by the endpoint signing secret); receivers enforce a five-minute timestamp tolerance and deduplicate the event_id across every generation. HTTP 2xx acknowledges; redirects are rejected; connect/read timeouts are bounded. Sealed outbound dispatch-status fanout is a separate deferred contract.

type.description: The event kind: one accepted sealed inbound event (kind 02).

event_id.description: The phone-allocated stable event identity (Q8); the receiver deduplicates on this value.

delivery_id.description: The delivery identity for this endpoint; changes across generations while event_id does not.

account_id.description: The account the event belongs to.

device_id.description: The capturing device named in the envelope's protected record.

observed_at_ms.description: Device-observed time from the protected record, Unix milliseconds.

envelope_b64.description: The exact stored sealed envelope bytes (standard base64). Ciphertext only: the relay cannot open it and never emits plaintext, a JSON body alternative or a downgrade flag (Q11).

unsigned_digest_b64.description: Standard base64 of the SHA-256 digest of the unsigned envelope bytes: the admission identity the receiver can compare against its own upload acknowledgment.

SealedUsage.description: One metering period from the durable usage core. Integer message counts only; never currency, invoices or pricing.

metric.description: The metered metric. Sealed outbound acceptance meters the shared outbound_message unit in v1; sealed acceptance does not introduce a second metric.

period_start.description: Inclusive UTC calendar-month start of the period (YYYY-MM-DD).

period_end.description: Exclusive end of the period and reset boundary: counters restart at 00:00 UTC on this date.

limit_units.description: The period's unit limit copied from policy when the period row was first created.

reserved_units.description: Units reserved by accepted messages in this period, one per accepted sealed envelope, reserved in the same transaction as admission.

refunded_units.description: Units refunded against reservations in this period by the pre-grant cancellation/expiry path; never exceeds reserved_units.

used_units.description: reserved_units minus refunded_units: the units this period has consumed.

Error.description: The existing error shape used by the message routes: a single machine-readable code and no content echo.

code.description: Lowercase snake_case machine code for the admission or resource failure; the response description defines the taxonomy.

SealedMessageMetadata.description: Stored delivery evidence, never inferred radio success. Existing sealed candidate rows currently admit only queued/cancelled/expired; grant transitions require the separate negotiated execution implementation.

SealedUsagePage.description: One bounded page of the account's usage history, newest period first, read from the single authoritative metering core (#631). consumed = reserved - refunded is a reservation counter and is never a submitted or delivered counter. An account without periods is a consistent empty page, not an error and not a distinction beyond emptiness.

next_before.description: Cursor for the next older page: the last row's period_start, or null when the history is exhausted.
